items.stem: By default, how do lists and libraries get their permissions in a SharePoint site?

options.text: They inherit permissions from the parent site
options.rationale: Correct: sites and content inherit from the parent until inheritance is broken.

options.text: Each item always has unique permissions
options.rationale: Unique permissions require explicitly breaking inheritance.

options.text: Permissions come from Azure Storage tiers
options.rationale: Access tiers are an Azure Storage concept, not SharePoint permissions.

options.text: Only the global admin can read them
options.rationale: Inherited permissions apply to assigned groups and users, not only the global admin.

items.explanation: Correct: sites and content inherit from the parent until inheritance is broken.

Correct: organization links work for internal users.

items.stem: Which site type is best for broadcasting news across an organization?

options.rationale: Correct: communication sites are designed for broadcasting news and status.
Channel sites support a specific Teams channel, not org-wide broadcast.
OneDrive is personal storage, not an org broadcast site.
A storage account is Azure infrastructure, not a SharePoint site.
